newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss institute forecast modest 1997 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Swiss institute forecast modest 1997 GDP growth.

text.p: Swiss economic research institute BAK lowered its forecast for 1997 Swiss Gross Domestic Product (GDP), but said recent data gave cause for optimism.
BAK forecast a rise of 1.0 percent for Swiss GDP in 1997, down from the 1.3 percent forecast in its last quarterly report from September.
Despite the lower forecast, BAK's forecast is still the most optimistic of those published for 1997 thus far and follows news last week that 1996 GDP fell by a real 0.7 percent.
The Federal Office for Economic Policy in Berne last week forecast 1997 GDP growth of just 0.5 percent. Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) has left its 1997 growth forecast at zero.

But Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) also said it believes the economy is nearing the end of its recession and that it will continue to stabilise in the months ahead, producing GDP expansion of 0.6 percent for all of 1997.
BAK said in its report that 1996 fourth quarter data showed a slight increase in overall economic activity as compared to the prior quarter.
It said the strongest growth this year is likely to come from the chemicals sector, with growth forecast at 4.9 percent.
In contrast, the agricultural is likely to experience a six percent contraction and the construction sector activity is forecast to shrink by 1.8 percent.
